subject: the Sun
title: The Sun Loses 4 Million Tons Every Second and Has Barely Noticed

scenes.text: Every second, the Sun gets four million tons lighter.
Fusion in its core turns that much mass straight into the light and heat that reach you.
The solar wind blows off another one and a half million tons each second.
Over four and a half billion years, that's more than 100 Earths of mass, gone.
Yet the Sun weighs 333,000 Earths. It has lost less than a tenth of one percent.
As it slims, its grip loosens, and Earth drifts outward about one and a half centimetres a year. Right now.

description:
The Sun converts more than 4 million tons of mass into energy every second, and the solar wind carries off about 1.5 million tons more.
Over roughly 4.5 billion years that adds up to more than 100 Earth masses, yet the Sun is 333,000 times Earth's mass, so it has lost only about 0.05%. Its weakening pull lets Earth's orbit grow by about 1.5 cm a year.
Did you know the Sun is getting lighter?
first_comment: At 1.5 cm a year, Earth needs about 65,000 years to drift one extra kilometre. What else in space is quietly changing?
